claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's art style, visual aesthetics, and graphics.

citations.review_text:
Hades is a visually stunning work of art with the gameplay depth to back it up. From the moment you begin your escape, the vibrant hand-drawn art style and dynamic lighting immediately grab your attention, making every biome feel meticulously crafted.

Beyond its breathtaking looks, the fast-paced combat loop delivers an incredibly satisfying experience. The core mechanics are quick to grasp, but mastering dodge timing, positioning, and weapon synergies takes real skill. Mixing different weapon aspects with randomized Olympian Boons ensures no two runs ever feel identical.

What truly elevates the game is how it turns the grind into pure enjoyment; even in death, earning permanent upgrades makes every attempt feel deeply rewarding. Hades hits the rare sweet spot where striking aesthetic beauty meets deep, addictive gameplay mechanics.
The best art direction and visual effect game ever created. It just feel so good every time you play it

claims.claim: Reviewers note that dying in the game advances the story and character progression rather than feeling purely punishing.

citations.review_text:
The only game i've seen that makes death not a punishment but an oppurtunity.
Yes, you can pet the dog.

The more I play this game, the more addicted I get: You fail a run, upgrade your stats with the items you collected, start a new run and get farther than before. Because you're able to progress the story after every run, failing doesn't feel punishing. On the contrary: Dying is part of the gameplay loop and lets you progress in the game. 

When chosing between items in runs you have to decide if you wanna go for the ones that help you in just that run or if you wanna think long term and fail that run earlier in favor of getting farther the following runs. My advice is to not focus too much on one run but instead to look at the game as a continuos voyage. Enjoy the journey!

As a huge fan of greek mythology I absolutely adore the love they put into each and every character. Together with the beautiful art style this truly creates one of the most unique games I've ever played.

citations.review_text:
I have an interest in Greek Mythology. One day, I saw this game on a discount and decided to buy it. 

Here's my story:
I'm not really much of a roguelike fan, but IMO this game does a pretty in introducing roguelike gaming to newbies like me. It's very intuative and as long as you want to get better at the game, everything becomes so easy to understand. This game makes it feel like every loss is your fault which incentivizes the player to understand what he/she did wrong. Like not paying attention to the enviroment, or not paying attention to the enemies, or just randomly dashing without thinking. All and all, the gameplay is very fun. As long as you're not a scrub, you'll get good.

The characters are also pretty cool. I like the artstyle in general. I haven't reach it yet, but I've also heard that you can "date" one of the characters (I hope I can date Medusa. God, just imagine that mouth on my di...) Ahem, anyway. What else? Oh, yeah. I also like how the characters react to your progress. I would've been easier and faster to just have the characters repeat the same lines over and over again. But I'm so glad Supergiant went the extra mile made lines for every major actions. Speaking of reactions, I also really appreciate how the inhabitants of the House of Hades feels like a family even the minor characters like The Contractor, The Broker, and Skelly feels like a part of the Court of Hades.

Either way, this game is very good. Highly recommended. I'm gonna go get lunch now.

VERY fun game.

Action-based combat is very fast, but you always feel like you're in control and it's comfortable. The Supergiant aesthetics and the dynamic OST mixing Greek and metal add to the experience. 

The story is the cherry on top - in other more popular roguelikes it's usually boring or non-existent, but here it's fully developed with THOUSANDS of voice-acted scripts of dialogue, all with witty humour in them. And, for my fellow non-Anglosaxon natives, the translations are just as good.

When you finish the game (should take you about 40 hours), the game is expanded even further with many more weapons for your character. Most importantly, it is also expanded with the "Heat" difficulty system, which is one of the most creative I've seen in any videogame. You can tweak any difficulty aspect you like (harder boss patterns, less item choices, more enemy health, timed runs...) and you can make thousands of different combinations.

So yeah, even if Hades II is out now, you can perfectly play this one for a more budget option.

[h2]METACRITIC SCORE -[/h2]  [h3]9.3/10[/h3]
[h2]MY ULTIMATE SCORE-[/h2]  [h3]9/10[/h3]

[h1]TLDR:[/h1]
[b]A very replay-able and fun game that is not too easy, but not too hard either.
With a touch of interesting narrative to keep you pushing towards the end, its addicting combat is all it really has, but with how fun and addicting that combat is, there is a reason why it is critically acclaimed.[/b] 


[h3]PROS:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Very engaging combat[/b] 
[*] [b]Rewarding progression[/b] 
[*] [b]Unique and cool setting- hell/hades[/b] 
[/list]


[h3]CONS:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]You will fight the same bosses and go through the same places over and over. They don't really "upgrade".[/b] 
[*] [b]You must rely on wiki or other sources to understand and pick the BEST choices. Game does not explain what symbols on doorways/rewards mean. You can learn on your own, but it will take longer than just having had a good guidebook/tutorial.[/b] 
[*] [b]You must successfully complete a run about 10 times to beat the game. Each time you do, the success is short lived, as you die from not being able to survive on earth, only in hades. This can feel like a cheap way for making you have to go through everything again, without any real reward besides some dialogue with a character.[/b] 
[/list]



[h1]NARRATIVE/STORY -[/h1]  [h3]8/10[/h3]
[b]This story is ultimately about patching things up between a father and son and mother.
It is told through dialogue, not through cutscenes.
Characters are well written, never feeling cheesy like some Nintendo games might (i do love Nintendo though!),
and they do have unique personalities.
This combination makes for a good time while having a real good reason to want to "escape hell", which is very intriguing.[/b] 



[h1]GAMEPLAY LOOP -[/h1]  [h3]10/10[/h3]
[b]Its just FUN. Addicting.
You also have variety, not only in what weapon you choose, but the "power-ups" that you choose throughout the game, so you can choose the playstyle that best suits yo…

Great game - combat, visuals and soundtrack but its annoying that the story is drip-fed to you. You need to complete 10 successful runs to finish the main story, though being asked to play more isnt really a bad thing. Also many more playthroughs are needed to reach the epilogue, the criteria of which isn't made clear...

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game incorporates story progression, dialogue updates, and character interactions into the repetitive run loop of a roguelike.

citations.review_text:
Alright, where do I begin? I was shown Hades after the hype of it through many friends, but one above all the rest was the most insistent I play it, so I caved in and gave it a shot. The game features this uniquely beautiful mix of 2D and 3D art styles taking place through the eyes of Zagreus, son of Hades. If it wasn't obvious by the name, the game is very heavily influenced by Greek mythology that is very much made their own; no game that comes to mind is even remotely close. The story of the game is very interesting and touches on some interesting ways to incorporate story into the almost infinite replay loop of your traditional roguelikes, from new dialogues, progression systems, and new mechanics to learn, to characters to meet, and even to something as peaceful as decorating your own home.

There is no shortage of content in this game and I can completely understand why it has received high praise for its bold choices and wonderfully composed music. I am very much looking forward to seeing where the sequel takes me and am definitely looking forward to future titles from Supergiant Games; if you're into roguelikes or just looking for something new for your palette, this game is for you.

8.9 / 10

This game has everything:
- Fun gameplay, with huge variability between runs with plenty of fun build options
- Interesting and deep characters, who react to what happened in your runs and develop over the course of the game
- A compelling, touching, and relatively low stakes story
- A beautifully done, well designed world
- Difficulty that grows with you after you've beaten the core loop of the game for the first time
- It starts naturally with relatively easy mechanics and controls and then grows more complex


The best part, however, is how Hades integrates all that:
- The Roguelite mechanics spring naturally from the setting of the underworld and the characters therein
- Everything you can find in the underworld makes sense to be there.
- How Zagreus interacts with other people and his reasons for doing what he does, comes naturally from who he is and his character. It makes perfect sense, why he, and not anyone else is on his quest.
- How you interact with characters and do dialogue, is perfect for a Roguelite
- The story and how it progresses is a perfect fit for a Roguelite

Hades is a near perfect game, especially because it feels so complete. Everything in it makes sense in the world of the game and is incredibly well tailored to the concept of a Roguelite.

This is a 10/10 for me, by far the best Roguelite I have ever played, and I would recommend it to anyone who is even remotely interested in this kind of game.

This game has quickly become one of my favorites in recent years.

I love how the story unfolds through bite-sized character interactions, both mid-run & at the main hub. It's also kind of cool to see characters interacting with you & each other, based on your current/past actions, objectives, or equipment. Makes it feel dynamic & leads to some pretty hilarious moments, even in the Boss rooms.

Though it is my first rogue-lite experience, there's something uniquely satisfying about going through a run each time. It scratches that gaming itch, when you want something short and uncomplicated.

Auto-saving happens after every room, so the game's easy to pick up/put down.
Death never feels like a complete failure because room rewards balance between temporary run boosts and permanent resources used to unlock weapons, upgrades, and story progression.

Another nice feature is the "God Mode" option, in the settings.
You can toggle it on/off any time to grant you a 20% damage resistance.
If toggled on, it increases the damage resist by 2% with each death (capping at 80% total).
There's no penalty or missed content/achievements for having it on the entire time.
Great for if you want to ease into the difficulty & can be turned off without losing accumulated resistance progress.

The SFX/audio design is pretty good.
Everything from weapon usage to boon/item pickups feels unique and tactile.
Plus, the OST's metal tracks go hard AF, especially for the bosses.

Definitely a solid experience & well worth every minute.

Hades is easily one of the best roguelike / hack and slash games I’ve ever played.

What pulled me in first was the setting. I’ve always been interested in mythology, gods, divine powers, and stories built around them, so this game immediately caught my attention. The way it uses Greek mythology feels stylish, creative, and full of personality. Every god, every character, and every interaction adds something meaningful to the world, making each run feel like more than just another attempt to escape the Underworld.

The gameplay is absolutely fantastic. Fast, smooth, satisfying, and addictive in the best way possible. Every weapon feels different, every boon can change your build, and every failed run still feels like progress. That’s one of the things I love most about Hades: even when you lose, the game still rewards you with story, upgrades, dialogue, and motivation to try again.

But what really makes the game special for me is Zagreus and the way he interacts with everyone around him. He isn’t just a silent protagonist trying to escape. He has personality, emotion, humor, frustration, and a real connection with the people in the House of Hades and beyond. His relationship with Hades is tense and complicated, but also one of the most interesting parts of the story. You can feel the conflict between them, not just as enemies, but as father and son.

At the same time, his interactions with characters like Nyx, Achilles, Thanatos, Meg, Cerberus, and the Olympian gods make the world feel alive. Every conversation slowly builds relationships, reveals more about the characters, and makes the Underworld feel less like a simple dungeon and more like a place full of history, emotions, and unresolved drama.

The story also surprised me with how captivating it is. It’s not just background lore thrown on top of gameplay — it’s deeply connected to every escape attempt. The relationships, the gods, the family drama, and Zagreus’ journey all make the game feel personal and mean…

💀🔥 Запомнится на века! 🏛️✨

Hades это:
- Отличная боёвка. Куча сочетаний и комбинаций божественных даров и адского оружия
- Выверенный темп игры. Сложно будет тогда, когда есть настроение, в ином случае можно сочно разносить врагов
- Богатый и глубокий сюжет. Безумное количество диалогов, мини историй и уместного юмора
- Отпадный дизайн. То чуство, когда богатства подземного мира затапливают экран

Прежде всего стоит сказать, что лучше в эту игру играть с гейпада, так как в таком случае лучше получается собирать удары в непрерывные комбинации наступления и уклонения. Не стоит расчитывать, что вы пройдёте весь сюжет быстро. Готовьтесь к тому, что вы дойдёте до сюжетной развилки быстро, а дальше это станет отличной игрой после работы, которая будет подавать сюжет ровными порциями после каждого забега. Я лично заходил с мысью "Ну-ка, что там в подземном царстве нового сегодня...". 

Прошёл полностью, закрыв все ачивки с большим удовольствием
Самая любимая rogue-like <3

Holy crap, what a fun game!
I've played other roguelikes or roguelites, and many are fun, but you wouldn't think a strong story is one of their strengths.  In the case of Hades: story, voice acting, dialogue are all very strong points of the game.  And of course it's addictive and so damn fun!
  It's like instead of playing the same story over and over again at higher difficulties just for bragging rights, here it's playing the same run again and again actually advances the story.  I wouldn't have thought of making a game that way if i were going to make my own, but Hades pulls it off and then some.
  Oh yeah and it definitely plays better with a controller rather than mouse and keyboard I'd say, so if you have one then check this game out!

[i]Very Good; but I question its S-Tier Status[/i]

The difference between good and exceptional status in my opinion comes down to elements that can seem a bit nitpicky; but I think that is what holds Hades back from the highest accolades.

First, I’d like to highlight the strong points of the title. The mythology theming is great and is continuous throughout all facets of the game including the ever-present story dialogs. The art style is also very visually pleasing. Combat feel and control is generally very good, which is essential since that is what this game is about 90% of the time. Enemy attacks and intentions are fairly telegraphed in most instances. Six different weapon types to select from; each offering solid variety from one another and a ton of boon enhancements to alter the playstyle. Also, the game makes good use of long-term progression currency sinks to keep you coming back run after run to make little improvements. 

Now for some of the areas that I think could have been better. The game requires a ton of repeated clears to advance the story to the conclusion; likely far too many for most players. The last biome seems considerably less developed than the prior zones. The interior areas are generally extremely small and the main obstacle generally becomes ground damage from poison spills or hard to see projectiles. Although not often an issue there are still times that the amount of screen effects makes it extremely difficult to see what the enemies are trying to do. 

The story element delivery is hit and miss and can get pretty repetitive constantly talking to every NPC each run and listening to the excess banter. However, I think it does work when placed at the end of a successful run giving that little extra incentive to keep completing clears.

In a similar vane to the large number of repeat clears; you cannot skip past difficulty level increases. Each +1-difficulty level has to be cleared progressively and they are weapon dependent. For example…

“In the name of Hades…”

I initially bought Hades during a sale. I played until I managed to beat a run once, then it ended up sitting in my backlog. I figured that since it’s a roguelike, I could always come back to it whenever I wanted. Fast forward a year, and I finally found the time to properly play it. And oh boy, I missed out on a lot of fun.

Hades is the first roguelike I’ve ever played. I was already familiar with the genre since I’d seen countless reviews praising roguelikes for their insane replayability, and Hades is no exception. I don’t know if it was because I was burnt out from school or just tired of the games I had been playing, but once I started, I genuinely could not stop.

The premise alone immediately hooks you in. You play as Zagreus, battling your way out of the Underworld while trying to solve a whole lot of family problems along the way. The game’s four regions each have their own distinct atmosphere. There are also environmental hazards unique to each area, like the traps scattered throughout Tartarus or the pesky lava covering Asphodel. These hazards add another layer to the combat and constantly force you to stay alert. 

My favorite region is probably Elysium. I absolutely love its vibrant green scenery, and I appreciate that after entering a new region for the first time, the game gives you a moment to simply admire the environment before throwing you back into the action. From the scorching heat of Asphodel to the satyr-infested Temple of Styx, there’s never really a dull moment. Ironically, there were times I found myself wishing for one because of how relentlessly fast-paced the game is. Spotting Charon’s shop or finally stumbling upon a healing fountain after surviving several chambers always felt like a well-earned breather.

Speaking of surviving, the enemies in this game deserve their own paragraph.

Every single one of them has found a unique way to piss me off.
